title: review follow-ups of PR #37900 (stdio bridge, disabled package)
body:
repo:objectstack#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibyUSf2nKJWW6qBemSU

Filing gate: ① L1/L2 follow-ups of one PR (`review follow-ups of PR #N`, one card per PR, later rounds append here). Source: fleet (L1 of PR #37900, comment 7215104549, item N1).
Grading: area:package · Task · p3 · domain:server. The ruled cell of #36689 (data) is closed by PR #37900; this is schema on a narrower host, outside that ruling.
Reader: seat repo:objectstack#3, zone o3-package, after PR #37900 merges (the files are the ones that PR changes).
Dedupe: `"PR #37900"` 0 hits; `list_objects disabled package` 23 hits, all closed and on other mechanisms (#25120, #25138, #25245 made the listing read the protocol's merged view; none covers a host with no protocol).

Business reason: when an admin disables a package, an AI client connected over a local MCP (stdio) session should stop seeing that package's objects, as it already does on a host with the protocol service. On a host with no protocol service the client still lists and describes them, so the model plans a query against an object whose data is then refused (after PR #37900). The cost is a wasted call and a confusing answer, not leaked data.

## Items
- [ ] N1: on a host with no protocol service, `list_objects` and `describe_object` (and the `objectstack://objects` resources, the same view) list and describe a disabled package's objects. The view falls back to `IMetadataService.listObjects()` / `getObject()` (`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts#stdioObjectView`, `#readMergedObjects` returns `undefined` there), which does not ask `isObjectPackageDisabled`. Expected: filter the fallback through the same predicate PR #37900 threads into `StdioObjectReads` (`isObjectPackageDisabled`), so a disabled package's object is absent from both tools and the resources on every host. Pin with a no-protocol-host test plus a re-enable control.

## Acceptance
- On a no-protocol host, a disabled package's object is absent from `list_objects`, `describe_object` answers not found for it, and the resources agree; re-enabling restores all three.
- The protocol-host behaviour is unchanged.
